items.title: ‘We are committed Christians’: Our son and daughter-in-law cut us off over politics. Should we change our $3 million will?
items.description: “We are hurt and confused, but we have also tried to respect the boundaries they have established.”

items.title: My father-in-law passed away, leaving a house with tenants. Do I evict them?
items.description: “We don’t know whether they have signed leases or are renting month to month.”

items.title: Global oil prices above $90 a barrel ahead of Bessent’s ‘economic D-Day’ announcement on Iran
items.description: What matters more for oil prices is how hard U.S. sanctions hit China, Iran’s biggest oil buyer, and whether Beijing pushes back.

items.title: U.S. automakers and home builders are among the big losers as Trump launches a trade war against Canada
items.description: While certain U.S. sectors are facing headwinds from the new tariffs on Canadian goods, analysts have said the broad economic effects of the new 50% U.S. levies could be modest for the U.S. overall.

items.title: Think Medicare Advantage provides better care for chronic conditions? A new study suggests otherwise.
items.description: Medicare Advantage enrollees with diabetes aren’t healthier than Americans on traditional Medicare — despite the grocery and gym perks.

items.title: ‘She looked into COBRA’: My friend was laid off and lost her health insurance. How can she find affordable coverage?

items.description: “Grandma feels that she was pressured by my mother into taking out a $50,000 HELOC.”

items.title: It’s time to bet big on Nvidia’s stock, says this analyst who thinks the market has it all wrong
items.description: Nvidia’s controversial financial plays could actually keep the company on top, according to this analysis.

items.title: ‘My main goal is to help people’: I’m single, 74, with $10 million burning a hole in my pocket. What should I do?
items.description: “I also own my home and an SUV outright, with no outstanding debt.”

items.title: Trump, Vance and Bessent try to calm the bond market with ‘alternative facts’
